nodes.title: Local-cohomology annihilator product
nodes.statement: For a commutative R, ideal J and R-module M, define a_J(M,d) = product over 0 ≤ j < d of Ann_R H^j_J(M). This is a finite product of ideals in R, not an intersection or the preimage of a product in R/Ann M. For the paper’s a(M), take J=m and d=dim Supp M when M≠0; the zero module uses the empty product, the unit ideal. The explicit finite cutoff avoids converting infinite or bottom dimension to a natural number.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring, M an R-module, J an ideal, and d a natural-number cutoff. No localness or Noetherian hypothesis is needed for this definition and its finite-product API.
proofSteps: Use the existing localCohomology J j functor on ModuleCat.of R M.
Take the finite ideal product; a dimension witness is supplied only when interpreting the paper’s notation.

acceptance: For every J and M, a_J(M,0)=1.
The cutoff-one product is exactly Ann_R H^0_J(M), not its radical.
All local cohomology of the zero module vanishes; every finite-cutoff product is 1.

Write A=Ann H⁰_J(M), B=Ann H¹_J(M). If AB differs from A∩B, then a_J(M,2) differs from A∩B. A concrete local example is M=k⊕R/(y), R=k[[x,y]]: A=(x,y), B=(y), so the product is (xy,y²), whereas the intersection is (y).

uses.how: Membership controls the next element on the actual prefix quotient.
Equidimensional support turns its zero locus into the non-CM locus.

nodes.title: CM-secant sequences
nodes.statement: For finite M over Noetherian local (R,m), an ordered list rs is CM-secant iff every term lies in m; every successive prefix quotient strictly lowers support dimension; the final quotient is Cohen–Macaulay; and for each index i the element rs_i belongs to a_m(M/(rs before i)M,dim Supp(M/(rs before i)M)). Empty rs is allowed and is CM-secant exactly when M is CM. The zero module admits only the empty list. Terminal CM is required only for the final quotient, so prefixes are not asserted CM-secant.
hypotheses: R is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; M is a finite R-module. The displayed sequence, dimension, duality and equidimensionality hypotheses are retained.
proofSteps: Expand the requested R03.3 secant predicate on native quotients by Ideal.ofList prefixes.
Express terminal CM by the requested Grothendieck vanishing criterion in terms of the native localCohomology functor; this is an expanded condition, not a competing generic CM definition.
Each nonempty prefix before a step has a finite natural support-dimension witness by Noetherian locality and Nakayama; record that finiteness comparison as a supplier need.

sources.match: Own formulation of cm-secant sequences, with the hypotheses and maps specified in this node; API consequences are derived from that construction.

acceptance: The empty list is CM-secant on the one-dimensional vector space over Q; its support has dimension zero.
[0] is not CM-secant on Q: the support dimension does not decrease.
The empty list is CM-secant on the zero module.
A nonempty list is never CM-secant on the zero module.
For R=M=Q[[X]], the singleton [X] is CM-secant: support dimension drops from one to zero and H^0_m(R)=0.
The singleton [X²] is also CM-secant on Q[[X]]; secancy is not restricted to a chosen uniformizer.

uses.how: Its initial prefixes satisfy three special sequence properties.
The full ordered list defines the prefix-product blowing-up ideal.

nodes.title: Dimension of the Rees algebra
nodes.statement: For every Noetherian commutative ring A and ideal J, dim A[Jt]≤dim A+1 in extended Krull dimension. For finite dim A this is the bound needed here; when dim A is infinite the inequality is automatic. No equality is asserted for J=0.
hypotheses: R is a commutative Noetherian ring and I an ideal. Dimensions are extended Krull dimensions, including bottom and infinity.
proofSteps: Noetherianity makes J finitely generated, so A[Jt] is a finite-type A-algebra by the native Rees finite-generation theorem.

First let A be a domain. A[Jt]⊂A[t] is a domain with fraction-field transcendence degree over A at most one. For every prime q of the Rees ring, Stacks 10.113.1 bounds ht q by ht(q∩A)+trdeg_A A[Jt]−trdeg_{κ(q∩A)}κ(q), hence by dim A+1. Taking the supremum gives the result; no universal-catenarity assumption is needed for this inequality.

For general A, map its Rees algebra surjectively to the Rees algebra over each minimal-prime quotient. The kernels are prime and their finite intersection is the Rees nilradical, since nilpotence is coefficientwise inside A[t]. Every prime contains one such kernel, so a prime chain is bounded by the corresponding domain quotient. Each base quotient has dimension at most dim A.
The zero ring and infinite-dimension cases use bottom/infinity conventions. This replaces the unread HIO dimension citation, rather than claiming that book was consulted.

nodes.title: The first local-cohomology claim
nodes.statement: In the inductive setup of Theorem 3.14, with local previous-stage chart (R′,M′), r_i and r_s both kill H^1_{(r_i,r_s)}(R′,M′).
hypotheses: R is a commutative Noetherian local ring and M a finite module. The ordered elements lie in m. The displayed weaker-prefix, CM-terminal or CM-secant assumptions are used exactly as stated; closed-point depth targets retain maximal chart primes over m.
proofSteps: Write I=I_{s−1} and use n>0. The reversed d-sequence makes r_s injective on IⁿM, hence on the previous-stage module M′ after homogeneous localization. Thus the two-generator Čech model gives H¹_(r_i,r_s)(M′)=colim_{m>0} H⁰_(r_i)(M′/r_s^mM′), with transition multiplication by r_s.

In degree n, the multiplication snake lemma gives 0→K_{m,n}→IⁿM/r_s^mIⁿM→Iⁿ(M/r_s^mM)→0, where K_{m,n}=(IⁿM:r_s^m)/(IⁿM+(0:_M r_s^m)) and the injection sends a class x to r_s^m x. Clause (ii) implies r_i and r_s both kill K_{m,n}. All n,m here are positive.

In the target graded module, homogeneous localization followed by degree zero gives the previous-stage blowup module for M/r_s^mM. The selected previous denominator r_i acts injectively on this image module in its localization (the module chart formula of §3.13). Thus its r_i-torsion is zero, and the exact sequence identifies the r_i-torsion of M′/r_s^mM′ with the localized kernel. This argument needs no unproved assertion that every quotient sequence remains CM-secant.
Both annihilators pass through the homogeneous localization and the filtered colimit. These are steps of the target proof, not additional roadmap targets.

nodes.title: The second local-cohomology claim
nodes.statement: In the inductive setup, assume the preceding-stage depth bound depth M′≥s−1 and the same bound for each actual preceding localized chart module of M/r_s^mM, m>0. Then H^j_{m′}(R′,H^{j′}_{(r_i,r_s)}(R′,M′))=0 for j<s−2 and every natural j′. Only j′=1,2 need argument: degree zero vanishes by regularity of r_i and degrees above two vanish by the two-generator Čech model. These are explicit outer-induction assumptions, not conclusions derived from the two annihilation statements alone.
hypotheses: R is a commutative Noetherian local ring and M a finite module. The ordered elements lie in m. The displayed weaker-prefix, CM-terminal or CM-secant assumptions are used exactly as stated; closed-point depth targets retain maximal chart primes over m.

The preceding-stage local-cohomology vanishing below s−1 is assumed for the actual localized chart of M and for the corresponding charts of M/r_s^mM for every m>0. The selected chart prime is maximal and contracts to m.
proofSteps: Use the explicit outer-induction input for the original module at a closed previous-stage point over m: depth M′≥s−1. For the two-generator Čech complex the degree-zero row vanishes because r_i is regular, and rows above two vanish by its length.

For row two, regular r_s gives H²_(r_i,r_s)(M′)=colim_{m>0}H¹_(r_i)(M′/r_s^mM′). The comparison to the previous blowup module M′_(m) of M/r_s^mM has r_i-killed kernel by (3.14.15), so principal H¹ does not see this kernel.

Use the second explicit outer-induction input for the actual previous blowup module M′_(m) of M/r_s^mM: its depth is at least s−1 for every m>0. The element r_i is regular on it, so its quotient by r_i^l has depth at least s−2 for l>0. Local cohomology commutes with both filtered systems. Thus colim_m colim_l H^j_m′(M′_(m)/r_i^lM′_(m)) vanishes for j<s−2, which kills row two in that range (3.14.16). The outer proof must justify prefixwise inheritance before providing this input; it is not inferred here from robustness on only the full terminal quotient.

Use the iterated local-cohomology spectral sequence E₂^{j,j′}=Hʲ_m′(H^{j′}_(r_i,r_s)(M′))⇒H^{j+j′}_m′(M′). Its abutment vanishes below s−1. With rows zero and above two absent and row two already vanishing in the needed range, the only possible incoming differential to row one has zero source; hence row one also vanishes for j<s−2.

nodes.title: Depth induction on prefix-product charts
nodes.statement: Under the weaker prefix conditions and a zero-dimensional terminal quotient, for every 0≤s≤t the module Bl_{I_s}(M) has depth at least s at closed support points over the closed point. One does not assert this bound at every point of the closed fibre. The support-dimension bound and proper/localization reduction then give the CM conclusion at the final stage.
hypotheses: R is a commutative Noetherian local ring and M a finite module. The ordered elements lie in m. The displayed weaker-prefix, CM-terminal or CM-secant assumptions are used exactly as stated; closed-point depth targets retain maximal chart primes over m.
proofSteps: Strengthen the induction hypothesis at stage s−1 to range over every finite module and eligible ordered list satisfying the weaker conditions and zero-dimensional terminal quotient. Its instances for M and M/r_s^mM are the ih and ihQuot inputs to Claim 3.14.6. Establish the full family of shorter-prefix conditions on these quotients, with canonical chart-quotient comparisons, before instantiating it; selected-prefix robustness alone does not do this. The missing prefixwise secancy/inheritance argument is recorded in the auxiliary-quotient induction gap. No dependency edge back to this node is used to hide the induction context.
For s=0 the depth lower bound is vacuous; for s=1 the principal chart is the quotient by r₁-power torsion, with r₁ injective on it.

For s≥2 work at a closed point and use the two-generator presentation, P=M′[T] and g=r_bT−r_a. One coefficient is module-regular, so multiplication by g is injective on P. The residual polynomial f is monic, so it is injective on every polynomial base change of a local-cohomology module.
Flat polynomial base change carries Claim 3.14.6 to P; then the long exact sequence for support enlarged by f raises the vanishing range to j<s−1. Claim 3.14.5 makes g act by zero on H¹_(r_a,r_b)(P).

Put N=P/gP. In N the ideal (r_a,r_b) acts as the principal ideal (r_b), so H²_(r_a,r_b)(N)=0. Write A₁=H¹_(r_a,r_b)(P), A₂=H²_(r_a,r_b)(P), and K=ker(g:A₂→A₂). The relation long exact sequence, with g zero on A₁ and surjective on A₂, gives 0→A₁→H¹_(r_a,r_b)(N)→K→0 and 0→K→A₂→A₂→0. Apply cohomology with support (m′,f) to the second sequence: the two A₂ terms vanish below s−1, so K does also. The first sequence then gives the same vanishing for H¹_(r_a,r_b)(N).

Quotienting N by r_b-power torsion leaves its principal H¹ unchanged. That quotient has no principal H⁰. The support spectral sequence now identifies its local cohomology with that of H¹_(r_b)(N), shifted by one, and hence gives vanishing below s. Localize at the actual closed prime (m′,f).

At the final stage, the zero-dimensional terminal quotient gives dim Supp M≤t by the height bound for an ideal with t generators. Equality holds for an actual secant system of parameters, but is not needed or asserted for the weaker hypotheses. The blowup support dimension is at most dim Supp M, whereas closed-point depth is at least t. Properness over the local base and localization therefore give CM everywhere on the support; regular-element reduction handles a positive-dimensional terminal quotient.

nodes.title: A CM ring whose maximal-ideal blowing-up is not CM
nodes.statement: For any field k, let A₀=k[x³,x⁵y³,x¹⁵y²,y⁷] and localize at its positive-generator maximal ideal m. Then A=(A₀)_m is a two-dimensional Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay domain, but Bl_m(Spec A) has a non-CM local ring. The chart at x³, after writing Y=y/x, is the localization of B=k[x³,x⁵Y³,x¹⁴Y²,x⁴Y⁷]; at n=(x³,x⁵Y³,x¹⁴Y²,x⁴Y⁷) its depth is one.
hypotheses: k is a field. The explicit base and chart localizations are at their positive-generator maximal ideals.
proofSteps: HJLS Example 3.6 gives this construction. Verify A₀ directly: with u=x³,v=x⁵y³,w=x¹⁵y²,z=y⁷, the presentation is k[u,v,w,z]/(v³−wz,w⁷−u³⁵z²). It is free over k[u,z] with basis vⁱwʲ, 0≤i<3, 0≤j<7. Reduction by the two monic relations gives spanning; distinct images are independent because x-exponents modulo 3 distinguish i and y-exponents modulo 7 then distinguish j. Thus u,z is a regular parameter sequence and A is CM of dimension two.

On the x³-chart, adjoin v/u,w/u,z/u. The change of variable Y=y/x gives a=x³,b=x⁵Y³,c=x¹⁴Y²,d=x⁴Y⁷, the displayed B. The homogeneous maximal ideal n contracts to m because the original generators become a,ab,ac,ad; hence this local chart survives base localization.

The equations b²¹=a²³d⁹ and c²¹=a⁹⁰d⁶ make B finite over k[a,d], so a,d are parameters. B is a domain, hence a is regular. The class of c² in B/(a) is nonzero: (28,4)−(3,0)=(25,4) is not in the exponent semigroup; Y-degree four forces two copies of c and x-degree at least 28.

Yet d c²=a b³c. The class remains nonzero after localizing at n: a denominator outside n has a nonzero constant term, whose monomial cannot cancel into the monomial ideal (a). Thus d is a zerodivisor on B_n/(a). A two-dimensional local CM ring would make every parameter sequence regular, so B_n is not CM and has depth one. This independently verifies the source example without using the uncleared HIO book.
